security_spec.violation_condition: OpenSBI M-mode SBI handler for sbi_covh_connect_device (COVH FID #1024 in new numbering) does not validate that the calling Supervisor Domain owns or has legitimate access to the IDE stream's upstream Root Port before establishing the SPDM session. The removed sbi_covh_register_rp() gate previously required the host to explicitly register RP MMIO ranges, which were cross-checked against the platform RoT TEE I/O manifest. In the new spec, this validation is offloaded to the RDSM via sbi_covt_program_rp_ide_stream, but connect_device itself no longer gates on any RP-registration precondition.
security_spec.summary: Removal of sbi_covh_register_rp() eliminates the explicit RP-ownership gate in connect_device; if the TSM handler proceeds to SPDM session establishment without verifying RP ownership or platform RoT manifest consistency, a malicious Supervisor Domain could bind devices through arbitrary Root Ports, bypassing TEE I/O topology enforcement

findings.finding: The sbi_covh_connect_device, sbi_covh_register_rp, sbi_covt_program_rp_ide_stream handlers and all CoVE-IDE (COVH/COVT) SBI extension code are absent from this OpenSBI repository. The SBI ecall interface header (include/sbi/sbi_ecall_interface.h) defines only standard SBI extensions (BASE, TIME, IPI, RFENCE, HSM, SRST, PMU, DBCN, SUSP, CPPC, DBTR, SSE, FWFT, MPXY) with no COVH or COVT entries. No CoVE-IDE ecall handler, SPDM session management, IDE stream descriptor, or root-port registration logic exists in any source file. The vulnerability described by the spec (privilege escalation via unvalidated IDE stream RP ownership in connect_device) cannot manifest because the attack surface does not exist in this firmware build.
